# t18.3 — SEC-H3: invisible codepoints subtracted from the charset allowlist by category

## Summary

`CustomInstructionSafetyValidator.containsOnlyAllowedCharacters` was a whitelist of 15 Unicode
**block ranges**. A block admits everything in it, not just what its author wanted from it. The
fix keeps the ranges and **subtracts a property** — nine Unicode general categories plus a
derived set of blank-rendering codepoints those categories cannot see.

Verified by exhaustive sweep of all 1,114,112 codepoints: the surviving problem set is **empty**
(was 37). Admitted set 33,478 → 33,441.

**Status: SEC-H3 closed. SEC-M7 closed. SEC-L10 half-closed** (see Findings).

## What changed

`src/main/java/.../domain/instruction/CustomInstructionSafetyValidator.java`

```java
public static boolean containsOnlyAllowedCharacters(String content) {
    if (content == null || content.isEmpty()) return true;
    if (!ALLOWED_CHAR_RANGE.matcher(content).matches()) return false;      // unchanged
    return content.codePoints().noneMatch(...::isDisallowedCodePoint);     // added
}
```

The second half is an **AND-narrowing**: it can only reject more, never admit more. Widening a
range in future cannot silently reintroduce an invisible character.

- `BLOCKED_CATEGORIES` — `Cf Cc Cn Co Cs Zl Zp Mn Me`. `Zs` deliberately absent (U+3000 and
  U+2000–200A are wanted). `\t \n \r` are `Cc` and exempted explicitly.
- `INVISIBLE_CODE_POINTS` — `{U+115F, U+1160, U+2800, U+3164, U+A8F9, U+FFA0}`. Blank-rendering
  but categorised `Lo`/`So`/`Po`, so no category mask can see them.
- `ALLOWED_CHAR_RANGE` made package-private so a test can measure range-only admission and
  prove the subtraction is not a no-op.

### The set was derived, not recalled

Swept the BMP against the JDK's own Unicode name tables (`Character.getName`). A hand-written
list of the "obvious" fillers would have contained five; the derivation found **six** —
`U+A8F9 DEVANAGARI GAP FILLER` was not on anyone's list, including security's recommendation.
`CharsetAllowlistSweepTest.pinnedSetEqualsUnicodeDerivedSet` re-derives it on every build and
asserts **exact equality**, so a JDK Unicode upgrade that adds a blank-rendering letter fails
the build naming it rather than quietly widening the control.

### Regression check on real content

`/tmp/t18_3/RepoImpact2.java` scanned **1,332 files** for codepoints admitted before and

### Mutation verification (ADR-0007 D7)

Snapshot/restore via `cp` from `/tmp`, never `git checkout` — that reverts to HEAD and destroys
in-progress work.

| # | Mutation | Killed by | Count |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | predicate back to range-only (the original defect) | all 4 rejection pins + sweep + `subtractionIsNotANoOp` | 6 |
| M2 | drop `NON_SPACING_MARK` from the category set | `combiningMarkRejectedFromRepository` + sweep | 2 |
| M3 | drop `0xFFA0` from the derived set | `pinnedSetEqualsUnicodeDerivedSet` + 2 filler pins + sweep + `subtractionIsNotANoOp` | 5 |
| M4 | **over-block**: add `SPACE_SEPARATOR` | `allowlistStillAdmitsLegitimateText`, `japaneseIsAllowed`, `ordinaryDefinitionTextStillAccepted` + 12 | 15 |

M4 matters as much as M1: it proves the rule cannot silently become *too strict* either. M1
correctly left the acceptance tests green, and M2 correctly left the derivation test green —
each mutant is killed by the tests that should notice it and no others.

## Findings

**1 MEDIUM (new evidence), 1 decision needing sign-off, 1 LOW half-closed.**

### The `Mn` block is a real tradeoff, accepted deliberately

Blocking `Mn` rejects NFD-decomposed kana and the handful of combinations with no precomposed
form (か + U+309A, Ainu セ + U+309A). Accepted because:

1. the rule applies **only** to `REPOSITORY_SUPPLIED` definitions; an operator needing those
   supplies the file via `--agents-dir`, which is `USER_SUPPLIED` and charset-exempt by design
   (ADR-0007 D3). `invisibleCharactersPermittedFromOperator` pins that escape hatch;
2. a combining mark modifies the previous glyph's rendering — the same class of mechanism as a
   bidi override. `指\u3099示` reads as `指示` to a reviewer and is a different string to the
   denylist;
3. measured cost on real content is **zero** (1,332 files, 0 regressions);
4. carving exceptions out of a category mask by hand is the defect being closed.

### SEC-L10 is half-closed

`ALLOWED_CHAR_RANGE` now has a test reference and is in the liveness enumeration.
`ALLOWED_MODEL_PREFIXES` is untouched — different constant, different class, and closing it
requires writing a test that exercises model-prefix policy. Left for a separate task rather
than widened into this one.

`BLOCKED_CATEGORIES` is deliberately **not** in the liveness list: the sweep test re-derives the
category rule independently instead of citing the constant, which is stronger than a name
reference. M2 proves it is live behaviourally.
